title: differential-headroom-tuner-and-decommit-safety-probe
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleet customers were seeing periodic decommits during sustained high-throughput bursts which caused partial SLA regressions for a small subset of tenants. Root cause analysis showed the existing static headroom model didn’t adapt quickly enough to shifted tail behavior and a conservative decommit path occasionally over-reacted during correlated utilization spikes.

This PR introduces two coordinated components: (1) a differential headroom tuner that continuously estimates per-pool headroom requirements using short and long-window utilization deltas, and (2) a decommit safety probe that probabilistically exercises a soft-failover path before accelerating decommit decisions. The goal is to reduce spurious decommits while bounding long-term capacity drift.

Design summary: the headroom tuner computes a per-pool headroom multiplier from two signals: an exponential short-window delta (30s) and a median long-window delta (10m). Multipliers are clamped and smoothed with a configurable hysteresis window. The decommit safety probe emits lightweight probe reservations (0-cost token reservations) to validate whether reclaiming slots will cause SLA slippage; probe failures increase decommit hold timers. Both components expose telemetry and parametrization through the existing autoscaler config surface.

Changes included: - autoscaler: add diff_headroom_tuner module with test coverage; integrate into allocate/reserve path. - controller: add decommit_probe controller that coordinates soft probes and influences scale-down votes. - telemetry: emit headroom_multiplier, probe_success_rate, probe_latency, and probe_inflight_count for per-pool dashboards. - helm: add new config keys and defaults to values.dedicated.yaml. - docs: ops runbook describing knobs, safe rollout steps, and SLO impact analysis.

Backward compatibility: all new behaviors are opt-in via feature flag and default to conservative fallbacks identical to current behavior. No config schema breakage.

Testing & validation: unit tests for tuner math and probe orchestration included. Integration test harness simulates sustained 95th-percentile load patterns and shows a 42% drop in scale-down-induced SLO regressions in local perf runs. CI initially surfaced linting and a flake in the probe timing test which were fixed in subsequent commits.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary fleet (5% of Dedicated pools) for 48h with closewatch alarms on per-tenant tail-99 latency and decommit-rate. If metrics remain stable, expand to 25% then 100% over two weeks. Automated rollback if probe_success_rate < 90% or decommit_rate increases by >25% over baseline.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration scenario - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated - [x] Docs runbook - [x] Feature-flag gated - [x] Helm config defaults added

Related: ENG-3245 (scale-down regression triage), SUP-9842 (customer incident: regressed latency after decommit), ENG-4018 (telemetry standardization).

review_comments: Julian Kwan: Please add a short note in the tuner code explaining the rationale for the 30s/10m windows and reference the perf numbers that informed those choices.
Maya Patel (author): Added comments and a link to the perf doc in the tuner module. Also added a small unit test that validates window edge cases.
Samir Desai: The probe path looks good but could cause bursty API traffic if probes are too frequent. Can we cap concurrent probes per pool and add exponential backoff?
Maya Patel (author): Implemented per-pool probe_inflight cap (default 3) and exponential backoff with jitter; added integration test to assert stable probe volume under churn.
Ava Thompson: CI reported a flake in probe timing on macOS runners; suggest tightening test timing tolerances or mocking clock.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in differential headroom tuner and a decommit safety probe to reduce spurious scale-downs; exposes telemetry for tuning; Helm knobs added. Recommended canary rollout and monitoring guidance included in docs.
